name: Bill Gates

summary.text: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft, left its day-to-day management in 2008, served as chairman until 2014 and stepped down from its board (and Berkshire Hathaway's) on March 13, 2020 to focus on the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. In United States v. Microsoft, Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson found in November 1999 that Microsoft held monopoly power in PC operating systems; his June 2000 breakup order was set aside by the D.C. Circuit in June 2001, which left the factual findings largely intact. Securities filings tracked by 13F services show the Gates Foundation Trust's largest holdings in 2025 were Microsoft and Berkshire Hathaway, with the trust cutting its Microsoft stake by about 65 percent in the third quarter of 2025.

facts.claim: On November 5, 1999 Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson issued findings of fact in United States v. Microsoft concluding that Microsoft held monopoly power in PC operating systems, with more than 90 percent market share, and that it had harmed consumers by distorting competition.
facts.quote: Microsoft, which held more than 90 percent of the PC operating system market share, caused consumer harm by distorting competition

sources.title: Findings of fact: Microsoft is a monopoly that hurts competition and consumers

facts.claim: On April 3, 2000 Judge Jackson issued conclusions of law finding that Microsoft had violated the Sherman Act and state antitrust laws, and on June 7, 2000 ordered the company split into operating-system and applications businesses. On June 28, 2001 the D.C. Circuit set aside the breakup order and remanded the remedy under a narrower scope of liability, while leaving the findings of fact largely intact and criticizing Jackson's out-of-court comments.
facts.quote: the D.C. Circuit affirmed Judge Jackson's findings of fact, but some of his conclusions of law were reversed

facts.claim: On March 13, 2020 Gates announced he was stepping down from Microsoft's board and from the board of Berkshire Hathaway, on which he had served since 2004, to spend more time on the Gates Foundation's work in global health, development, education and climate. He said he would remain a technology adviser to CEO Satya Nadella. He had left his day-to-day role at Microsoft in 2008 and served as chairman until 2014.
facts.quote: He left the Microsoft board entirely as well as his seat on the board of Berkshire Hathaway

facts.claim: According to a 13F tracking service, as of June 30, 2025 the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust's largest stock holding was Microsoft at about $13.03 billion (roughly 27 percent of the portfolio), followed by Berkshire Hathaway at about $11.72 billion and Waste Management at about $7.375 billion; during that quarter the trust bought about 6.95 million Berkshire Class B shares and sold about 2.27 million Microsoft shares.

sources.title: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation Trust 13F Activity & Position Changes (Q2 2025)
Bill Gates Leans Heavily On Warren Buffett's Playbook, Pumps More Into Berkshire

facts.claim: Reports on the trust's third-quarter 2025 13F filing say it cut its Microsoft stake by 65 percent, selling 17,000,000 shares, and sold 2,358,460 Berkshire Hathaway shares for about $776 million; the portfolio's value fell from $47.78 billion at the end of the second quarter to $36.58 billion at September 30, 2025, leaving Berkshire (about 29.9 percent), Waste Management, Canadian National Railway and Microsoft (about 13 percent) as the largest positions.
facts.quote: The most dramatic change was a 65% reduction in its Microsoft Corp. stake, with the trust selling 17,000,000 shares.

facts.claim: In a 1983 interview quoted by The Register, 86-DOS author Tim Paterson recounted that the operating system became Microsoft's property on July 27, 1981, with Seattle Computer Products able to see the source code but otherwise just another licensee; The Register put the total Microsoft paid for the system at roughly $50,000 to $75,000. Paterson left SCP in April 1981 and joined Microsoft the following month.
facts.quote: the operating system became Microsoft's property on 27 July 1981

openQuestions: Site claim (Crash Conduits): Mary Maxwell Gates sat on United Way's national executive committee with IBM chairman John Opel and discussed her son's company with him in 1980. Not found in any source opened.

Site claim: Microsoft licensed 86-DOS for about $25,000 in late 1980 and bought all rights for $50,000 in July 1981. The July 27, 1981 purchase is supported by Paterson's account in The Register; the $25,000 and $50,000 figures appeared only in Wikipedia entries and were not recorded.

Site claim: Seattle Computer Products later sued Microsoft alleging it concealed the IBM relationship and the dispute settled for about $1 million. No source for the lawsuit or settlement was found in this research.
The 13F figures come from tracking services and news sites, not the filings themselves; the trust's filings on EDGAR should be checked, and later quarters (Q4 2025 onward) were not retrieved.
The D.C. Circuit's 2001 opinion and the Justice Department's case page were not among the pages returned; the appellate summary rests on secondary accounts.
